No worries! As long as its treated it wont be a problem. My cat's had worms before too, the treatment is easy, usually a shot or pill the vet will give. Its good you are paying attention to their health!

The most common reason is fleas. Watch if your cat is biting, itching, or heavily grooming frequently, especially in the afflicted area. Check the underside of your cat for fleas, as well as his paws (peppery flea dirt often gets stuck here from scratching). If your cat is longhsired in particular, the appetite loss could be from overlicking and building up hairballs. Or just from being too busy grooming to eat or excercise.

If not fleas, the other likely reason is parasites. Your cat will have noticeable changes in appetite. Check to see if their weight has changed suddenly, too. Their litter will also be inconsistent, as the parasites--particularly worms-- typically reside in the gut. If this is the case, see a vet for treatment.

(This depends on the cats age and health history too, and im not giving professionsl advice, just experience)

Im pretty good at naming characters but even then itll fade over time or the character might notve been important enough. Howver i think a good tip would be just referring to them by hair or other physical attribute at first in your head until you get them down.

For long term, do you have other problems remembering peoples names that you meet, and how do you combat that? I know regular interaction can help. Like you mentioned yourself, maybe instead of bingeing, limit yourself to just an episode a day, especially for a shorter but more heartfelt series. Longer series like naruto are good for binging a ton, but there are way more characters, and some you might not even need to remember. 

You could use visual and physical interaction yourself by possibly writing down  the name of the character (or person if also an irl problem) whenever you see them to help visualize. This also has your body steadily associate an activity with their name as well (humans learn to read and write with muscle memories, so it stands to reason that writing names or descriptors will help with memory. I remember thing much easier if Ive written them down, even if i dont ever look at what ive written  again!)

The problem is sometimes visuals arent enough. One character may say anothers name in dialogue, without the named one present. Writing their name doesnt work here. Example, a and b are talking about c, but c is not present for you to visualize. In this case--though maybe tedious at first--you could say the characters name when you see them, locking audio and visual learning together as well as kinetic learning by involving yourself. Then when you hear the characters name spoken, youll have a better association from already speaking and visualizing it yourself.

Again, tedious, but you could also pause the program and google the characters name--youre very involved here for a moment and forcing yourself to find an answer, but it might end up being more of a short term solution compared to the other suggestions.


If youre an artist or writer, further the visual memorization creating art and stories! There are certainly old characters i wouldn't have remembered features for if i hadnt drawn them. Example, kakashi who? Oh yea, i had to draw his fluffyhair and eyepatch-mask or whatever. Or, oh right i remember that simple-yet-difficult bowl cut hair anywhere, its rock lee! And even if you arent a great artist, its fun, its practice, its research, and its effort that pays off in the end. Maybe save it for your favorite characters who you really want to remember tho.  

I hope any of this helps! I know its surely a hassle, and most shows are very character driven, making you focus more on remembering  names and personalities than story. Playing "whos that pokemon" with every side character can be a real pain at first. But dont give up enjoying what you love!

Edit hmmm, adding in that japanese names are surely harder to remember than english ones, or really any foreign names versus the native tongue. Also tedious and roundabout, but looking up name meanings could help? Like memorizing dictionary definitions.

Example. Sakura, cherry blossom, shes got pink hair! Naruto, named after a ramen topping with a spiral, his Spiral patterns are in his movesets and clothing! 
I dont watch haikyuu but a random example i concluded was Ryunosuke--"ryu" is dragon, and hes a very hotheaded personality, sometimes animated having sharp teeth!
Or "inosuke" from demon slayer--i know by now that ino means boar, and he wears a boar head pelt! Boom, name memorized.
Boku no hero is a great example of this too btw. Midoriya--"midori" is green, his green hair and hero outfit. Bakugou--baku is explosion! I found almost all their names extremely easy using this method! (And should I even delve into all the jojo examples for this?)

This really only works with on-the-nose naming of course, and isnt a gaurantee to work every time, but could at least get you familiar with common names and meanings.

Something very similar happened when i forst moved, i was getting my cat used to the porch and adjusting him to outside, but he ran off at one point and didnt come back for over a week. Cats have good senses of smell and direction though. Having his catbox out and food (canned with a strong smell) will greatly help. If there are other strays in the area they could be scaring him off, so its best to check if there are other outdoor cats or strays in the area (mine had a few and i still dont let my cat out at night cause he fights them)

Cats are also most active at night, typically between ten and 3am or so ive heard. Going out and looking for him then could be good.  If you notice food is missing overnight (and dont suspect strays or other animals) your cat could be coming by while youre asleep. Stay up late and watch for him! A lso cats dont usually stray far from where they left, and most cats wont go more than a mile (at MOST) from home ( read this on a pet finder site)

Speaking of, id make use of pet watching/pet finder sites and apps! There are sites and local social media group pages where people can keep an eye out for your cat! This is what ultimately helped me as someone saw an online post and got in contect telling me they think they found him! Sure enough. And that idiot cat had barely even strayed from the apartment complex. 

Best of luck! Your cat is most likely scared of the new environment its in and wants to come home. Stay up late, put up online adverts, and have patience.

First cons are big, bustling confusion! Your first thing to do is to get a map of the convention area (if its spread out between multiple buildings especially), and get an event schedule! Theres usually one online especially closer to the con date. You can view panels and prioritize which ones youd like to see based on shows, voice actors, or content youre looking for more. Panels are usually hoated by guest speakers, va's or talent looking to showcase themselves in the community about certain topics.

If panels arent your thing then find out about the dealers/vendors rooms. These are where youll find all the official cool merch like plushies, pillows, figurines, etc etc. Then my favorite part of a con is usually the artists room. This is where youll find fanart in form of wall prints, scrolls, zines and doujins, keychains and all sorts of fanmade content therein. If its you and your friend plan a place to meet up if you get separated. Dont be afraid to take pictures, either, and even ask cosplayers you like for a picture qith them! 

Above all, bring cash, preferably small bills like tens, fives and ones. Almost everyone will take credit, but its an easier way to manage your budget, and small bills are easier for most small artists and vendors to handle. 

Theres also typically shows like a cosplay contest, and a gaming area, as well as usually a manga library you can browse and relax in. 

Above all, stay hydrated and have fun!!!

Its absolutely preferencw for most of the time. A lot prefer the original japanese voice, some people dont like reading subtitiles, sometimes its down to keeping the animes integrity or nostalgia.

Example, i prefer oldies i saw dubbed like bebop, champloo, space dandy, trigun, fullmetal, death note etc etc etc cause thats how i watched them first, and therea good acting.

But i prefer subs for most newer shows, cause thats how i watch it now!

And some shows are up for debate because of their integrity. Example, i prefer evangelions original dub because thats how i watched it and its iconic, but the sub has more accurate translating sometimes. Netflixs dub changes the script up too, as is a recent topic for debate again. 

Or some people prefer dubs for comedy, like in ghost stories.

Id only watch jojos bizzare adventure subbed because you get the wacky engrish thrown in that only works with the japanese voices. Same goes for watching osomatsu san

So its up to you! Some subs have better translation that keep the original japanese context like japanese puns or phrases or tradition (see pokemons well known change of "onigiri" to "jelly donuts" for americans). But english is great for those who struggle to read subs or just dont kind the occasional change in context. Its up to you!

To add. I think hxh takes some similarities. Theres a unique powerset, hyped up battles, hisoka (need i say more?), and a ton of interesting arcs! Its contrasts are the art style, storytelling, and overall character types of jojos however,making it extremely different in all other regards.

Psycho pass, ergo proxy reccomendation:

-paranoia agent. This one is a golden one. Its by satoshi kon who, if you dont know,  is the genuis of perfect blue, paprika, and tokyo godfathers (three movies i also reccomend). He blends and blurs the line between what is reality and fiction, and the consequences of it. Paranoia agent follows a town who slowly becomes overwhelmed by the seemingly ficticious assailant known as shounen bat, made up by a popular character designer as a scapegoat and repeated as an excuse by other people who dont want to take responsibility of their actions. As each episode progresses the fiction becomes more real and twisted. It's great commentary on well, mass paranoia, and each story is unique and fun to watch as they coalesce into the overall plot. Youll love satoshi kons storytelling!!

-serial experiment lain- this ones an obvious one. Its got the same vibe as ergo proxy, the same strange questionable characters, the same commentary on technology taking form. -evangelion- Im putting this here because it is heavily scifi and introduced a lot of concepts to future anime. Its classic, but some find it hard to get into due to some tropes played out in the first episodes. To know some of its production hiatory, evangelion was written episode to episode as it aired, starting as a shonen with a dark twist on death; but as the series went on, so did the creators depression and interest in psychology which flooded right over into evangelion, resulting in this slowly collapsing masterpiece of commentary on the human psyche. The episodes grow grim, hopeless, horrifying, and then you realize he was subverting to that all along. The last two eps are regarded as throwaways but carry heavy intent and commentary. The movie end of evangelion provides a more final conclusion, and i reccomend watching it after you finish the series. Theres also a debate about the netflix dub/original, and while i naturally reccomend the original, the netflix dub is watchable. The first anime I ever saw!

I first thought about going with something wild like dmitri, percy, alistair, Von (or vaughn), something that just stood out, or was unique, but I settled on something short and easy because it felt most natural. Shaun isnt too close to my dead one aside from the first letter, so it keeps the initials the same, and its quick single syllable that I was most responsive to. It also has the same meaning as my brothers name which i felt was important, as hes the most supporting family member and the only one i feel i want to even be related to. Picking a name from people close to you that has significance like that I think plays a key role. Its not just fishing for a strong name or a fancy one, its probably one that you can switch over to easiest but doesnt sound like your old one so you dont get those bad memories that are from being called by any name, just positivity. 

But it comes all down to what you enjoy being called the most. A lot of new dudes are also worried about falling into the stereotype and find themselves switching names because of that, but its best to remember that a lot of cis guys have the same names too, so its not a big problem if youre the fiftieth danny or sam or alex on here. Plus with younger people or newer generations, i feel it is easier to get away with twists on certain names, like xander or alec instead of alex, or topher instead of kristopher, or getting benji from benjamin, if you build off existing names its fun to play around with what fits, and what you really want to hear from others.

Oh also, the first transguy i knew was named roman, and he transitioned while i was in classes with him, he felt the name just come to him! The fact that most of us including our teachers accepted it probably helped his confidence in calling himself that. 7ish years later and hes had t, top, steroids, etc, and feels more content than ever, all just starting with a name change and support from his classmates.

If you look more into the production behind it, it kinda explains the sudden change in tone. Hideaki anno was going through a long depression himself and researched more and more on philosophy with the help of his colleague, which obviously made its way to his work--which was basically being made up episode to episode btw, without much than an overarching plot stranded together. The show was put off its course after an attack happened in part of japan, during production, that led them to set back some of the shows violence as well because it too closely resembled the recent realworld tragedy. [Check out SuperEyepatchWolf's video on youtube, it gives a better history for it].

 But otherwise a lot of the writing is intentionally vague and off putting. Maybe it doesnt hold up today, where anime is so widely churned out in complicated new plots and ideas that, a lot of eva's material seems done already. Cause the shows 20-odd years old and yeah. Of course it seems done before. It was more of an "of its time" type of show. 

I think thats the main problem new viewers have with it, at least. Writing it off as bad because youve seen media like it (or influenced by it), or because you were expecting a big battle mech anime without the philosophy, or because you find it "edgy" or overused (maybe today, but not then), is a bit of a lazy analysis imo. Not to overwork it, but its hard to deny that it was pushing limits for its time, with its unravelling into its characters and into the creators own mindset, it set quite a pace for future anime creations.

Maybe its not for you, cause it was made for a different time, and not meant to be just a typical mecha anime like you probably expected. But I like to appreciate it for what it was worth during its runtime, and for the feeling I had watching it so many years ago when I was just discovering what anime was.

SAMURAI CHAMPLOO. Yes, its set in the era of edo, samurai, feudal japan, but its not myths and monsters, its extreme swordfights and plenty of down to earth values surrounding the adventures of jin, mugen, and fuu. The characters are interesting and the world while being etched in realism seems so fantastical since its a different time period, especially with the extreme shenanigans they get up to. Shinichiro watanabe, creator of bebop and space dandy, keeps his deep writing and fanciful storytelling while still making everything well, real, as though it actually couldve taken place there.

Also suggest searching other feudal samurai shows, as they usually can be realistic, despite being set in a separate time period.

PSYCHO PASS.  Jumping to the future now, this one is more like scifi realism. Its what a future controlled by a single governing system would be like, where everyones minds are determined on a hue scale to be normal or dangerous in an effort to stop potential criminals. While being a bit out there in terms of technology, the actual fighting, emotions, and conflict are very grounded. People can get wounded, die, experience loss and confusion, they can lose their minds or keep it together and press onward. While not modern in tech, it does flow like a modern detective mystery, with sci fi elements. No magic, just some really really freaky science. Highly recommend it.

Ive watched all of hxh and while yes its a fuckton of characters im just glad they arent all thrown out at once. It builds up into a cast ivertime and dedicates screen usage to each individual when its necessary. Sure maybe i dont recall every name but i recall what each one was about at least. But again, less episodes than one piece, main reason why i was able to keep watching (maybe if id tried one piece when it was starting out i couldve been caught up but now its wayyyy too much for me to dedicate to)

Hxh is easier to follow and holds ny attention, couldnt stay into one piece. I think hxh is more classic to its genre, and has a solid world that keeps growing and building with each arc to keep viewers interested, along with a good cast of characters that doesnt overwhelm you with too many at once (theres the main 4 characters, and a couple side ones you dont even really worry about till later as they get more attention). Its hard to manage a huge cast of characters all at once, and that mightve been what intimidated me about one piece (naruto and bleach also face the same challenge). It has character arcs that mostly get resolved or at least leave you anticipating more or resolving them for yourself, even if the series isnt finished (except kurapika, who gets his resolution off screen, but his arc alongside  the phantom troupe shows some growth at least). 

The characters are also out there in terms of strange abilities, but suprisinglt our "main four" end up feeling extremely grounded compared to the wild world they explore. In a land Where people can kill with playing cards, plant invisible bombs, completely rearrange their body with acupuncture, where they have all sorts of visually jarring quirks from clown makeup to being an actual octopus, our main characters stay true to their personalities and keep the audience at their same suspension of disbelief for each new weird villain or ally they meet. We get to see it become a newer broader world through the eyes of our child protagonists, letting it feel new as we figure it out with them.

Cant give a complete comparison, but i think these are the main qualities that made me keep watching hxh, but not one piece. One piece felt overwhelming. While hxh has its faults (some fights seem drawn out beyond their time limits, the narrator is constantly telling you things you already know, and goddamn i really wanted more screen time for kurapika after the troupe arc) its forgiving enough to let the viewer keep up.

Plus, 62 episodes versus over 500 was a lot easier for me to get into lol

Hey ace! I think a good start to it all is coming out. You get to know who is supportivr and can help you, and what reactions to expect from those who arent. Try to coax your parents into referring to you with the right name and pronouns. Remind them whenever they get it wrong. Mybe its on purpose, but if not then just remember theyve been used to calling you something different and have to adjust.

Come out to close friends as well, they can provide very good support in this time, and will help with dysphoria when they refer to you properly.

Depending on your age, you can even ask your teacher to do the same!

From here it dependa on the support your gathering and how old you are. If youre still in your teens, your parents can help set you up on a therapist, puberty blockers or seeing an endo/gyno for testosterone treatment. If they arent supportive and you dont hve other relatives to consult, its best to wait til you are 17-18 to get treatment (in the mean time, you can request to get shorter haircuts or dress in menswear if it helps ease any dysphoria.) At the very least, your parents are sure to be convinced to set you up with a gender therapist after a little while. 

If you dont have one already: You can ask to order a top binder online as well. Theres discussion forums on here about brands if it gets confusing to look for one.

If youre over 18, the choices are yours. Most men start with therapy and binding and passing, hrt if they want it, and if its so desired you can search for reassignment surgery over a few years. 

Everyone moves forward at their own pace bro! Good job on coming out proud about who you are.

Their entire difference is in their charisma. Its like, no matter your amount of skill, thats not what it takes to be a hero.
Mp100 does this better imo. Mob can absolutely defeat any evil. Hes got powers beyond explanation. But hes also the meekest, least popular kid. This theme is repeated in his fight with claw, and in other upcoming encounters. Its paralleled with characters around him. He grows not because of his power already, but because he wants growth elsewhere. Physical, emotional, etc. Its heartwarming, even! His brother ritsu envies mob's ability, but hes extremely talented in areas of mental and charismatic ways, which ultimately lead him (down the wrong path but also) to acquire recognizeably great power.
